course.title: Android Development — Complete Deep Mobile Development Course
course.description: A Android Development-specific, beginner-to-advanced mobile development course with detailed UI, state, networking, persistence, authentication, testing, performance and production release lessons.
course.curriculumPolicy: Module and lesson counts are determined by the concepts required to learn the platform properly; no fixed cross-mobile template is imposed.
learningOutcomes: Test, optimize and prepare production releases.
Build a complete learning-platform mobile client.

modules.title: Android Foundations & Project Structure
modules.description: Android Studio, Gradle, app modules, manifests, resources, activities and the Android project lifecycle.

lessons.title: Android Foundations & Project Structure
lessons.description: Android Studio, Gradle, app modules, manifests, resources, activities and the Android project lifecycle.
learningObjectives: Apply it to a real mobile learning workflow.
Handle state, lifecycle and errors correctly.

notes.text: Android Studio, Gradle, app modules, manifests, resources, activities and the Android project lifecycle.

Learn android foundations & project structure by understanding the mobile-app problem first, then the framework concept, then a small implementation, and finally how it fits into a production learning application.

Android Foundations & Project Structure is important when building a reliable mobile learning experience. Students should understand not only how to make the screen work, but also state, lifecycle, networking, performance, accessibility and production behavior.

notes.alt: Android Development Android Foundations & Project Structure visual
notes.caption: Add a mobile architecture or UI diagram showing Android Foundations & Project Structure visually.

items: Handle loading, empty and error states.

notes.code:
Scenario: Create the foundation of a modern Android learning app.

Flow: user action -> UI state -> application logic -> data source -> result -> updated UI.

items: Define the state and data boundary.
Test loading, success and failure states.
Test different screen sizes and accessibility.
Putting all state into one component.
Blocking the UI with synchronous work.
Building only for one screen size.
Keep UI and data responsibilities separated.
I can explain Android Foundations & Project Structure in my own words.
I can implement a small example.
I can explain the data/state flow.
I can handle a failure state.
I can explain one production concern.
